sourceReferences.label: Torn Organized Crime 2.0
sourceReferences.notes: Used as structural inspiration for planning/execution phases, role slots, tools, materials, member counts, and branching outcomes.

rankScale.label: F
rankScale.notes: Low-stakes local work or apprentice contracts.

rankScale.label: D
rankScale.notes: Routine field work with manageable danger.

rankScale.label: C
rankScale.notes: Requires trained members, decent kit, and real risk management.

rankScale.label: B
rankScale.notes: Serious contracts with meaningful failure costs and branch complexity.

rankScale.label: A
rankScale.notes: High danger or political sensitivity with specialized role expectations.

rankScale.label: S
rankScale.notes: Exceptional operations intended for later high-end authored content.

riskScale.label: Low
riskScale.notes: Minor injury, schedule slip, or local reputation loss is the main failure cost.

riskScale.label: Moderate
riskScale.notes: Combat, legal trouble, or meaningful financial loss is plausible.

riskScale.label: High
riskScale.notes: Major injury, mission collapse, or faction blowback is expected on failure.

riskScale.label: Severe
riskScale.notes: Permanent losses, deaths, or serious political fallout are credible outcomes.

checkKinds.notes: Flat stat gate or weighted stat contribution.
Rank-based check against an authored player skill.
Presence of a learned active ability unlocks a bonus path or mitigation.
Presence of a spell grants a bonus branch, safety net, or alternate route.
Special tool or kit requirement that may or may not be consumed.
Consumable, reagent, or cargo item requirement.
Equipment class or slot tag needed for the route.
Crew size can help or hurt depending on noise, load, or formation pressure.

records.name: Reef Soundings Charter
records.summary: Brineharbor's harbor office needs a fresh sounding route through a reef shelf that shifted after the last storm surge.

notes: Protect and good route reading reduce weather losses.
At least one deployed character should handle rough-water recovery and skiff work.

classification.failureProfile: Skiff damage, lost charts, and temporary harbor penalties are more likely than total party loss.

roleSlots.label: Navigator
roleSlots.notes: Handles charts, tide tables, and route calls.

roleSlots.label: Sounding Hand
roleSlots.notes: Drops lines, checks reef markers, and recovers if the skiff grounds.

partySizeRules.effect: Fewer hands increase the time spent on recovery branches and reduce the margin for weather errors.
Extra crew helps only if the launch stays quiet; too many people raise grounding and noise risk in the shallows.

miscNotes: Storm RNG matters more on spring and harvest tides.
A critical success can permanently reduce later coastal travel risk on this lane.

nodes.label: Plot the tide window
nodes.summary: Choose the launch time and path through the shifting reef shelf.

checks.notes: Route knowledge and tide reading are the primary charting check.
Reading tide charts correctly.
Improves weather tolerance and steadies the crew in bad chop.
Spring winds can still spoil the best plan.

criticalSuccess.summary: You catch the cleanest tide and trim hours off the run.

success.summary: The crew launches on a workable route window.

failure.summary: A bad route guess runs the skiff shallow before the real work begins.

criticalFailure.summary: The launch window collapses into breakers and the office recalls the charter.

nodes.label: Sound the channel
nodes.summary: Work the lines and marker buoys while the reef remains half-exposed.

checks.notes: Recovery and line work in bad water are extraction-heavy tasks.
Precise marker drops and line work.
Too few hands slows the sounding pattern.
Unexpected surge between reef teeth.

success.summary: You finish the chart and clear the shoal before the next swell cycle.

partial.summary: You recover usable charts, but one section remains rough.

failure.summary: A grounding forces the crew into a desperate recovery loop.

nodes.label: Recover after grounding
nodes.summary: Free the skiff, salvage the lines, and decide whether to continue or limp home.

checks.notes: Getting the hull off the reef.
Treating cuts and coral scrapes keeps the crew working.
Reduces further injury while working the hull free in surf.
The sea may hit the hull again before it comes free.

success.summary: The crew salvages enough work to complete the charter at reduced pay.

failure.summary: The reef wins; the crew abandons the launch and the office voids the job.

nodes.label: File the soundings
nodes.summary: Return the finished route notes to the harbor office and collect payment.

checks.notes: Good reporting may convert a rough chart into partial harbor reputation.

success.summary: The harbor office accepts the chart and logs the lane.

records.name: Ore Train Relief Run
records.summary: Ironwheel Haulage needs a reinforced crew to move a delayed ore convoy through a switchback corridor before the smelter shift goes cold.

notes: Defender, Provoke, and Protect are strong mitigators on the ambush branch.
More bodies help with load and axle recovery, but increase the convoy profile on the ridgeline.

classification.failureProfile: Broken cargo, team losses, and reduced business trust if the ore misses the furnace window.

roleSlots.label: Wagon Master
roleSlots.notes: Calls route pace, spacing, and load order.

roleSlots.label: Guard Line
roleSlots.notes: Screens the convoy and reacts to road pressure.

roleSlots.label: Field Fixer
roleSlots.notes: Handles axle, harness, and brake failures.

partySizeRules.effect: Understaffed crews struggle to hold the line during the ambush and axle-repair branches.
Large crews move the cargo safely but increase detection and food consumption on long climbs.

miscNotes: This quest treats more people as mostly good in the repair branch and only mildly bad in the concealment branch.
Failure leaves a visible ledger flag on Coppergate industrial employers.

nodes.label: Stack the wagons
nodes.summary: Decide what rides high, what rides protected, and how the escort rotates around the convoy.

checks.notes: Good load balance prevents axle strain.
A fixer can brace the weak axle before departure.
More hands help secure and lash the load.

success.summary: The convoy rolls out balanced and ready.

failure.summary: A wheel starts to drift before the convoy clears the first ridge.

nodes.label: Hold the switchback
nodes.summary: Bandits and falling rock force the escort to protect the lead wagons through a narrow climb.

checks.notes: A disciplined front-line weapon line controls the road edge.
Draws raiders away from the wagons.
Reduces attrition on the climb.
Loose stone can still wreck formation.

criticalSuccess.summary: The escort breaks the ambush cleanly and reaches the furnace road early.

success.summary: The convoy takes hits but remains intact.

failure.summary: The line holds, but a wagon axle snaps under pressure.

nodes.label: Repair the axle under pressure
nodes.summary: Fix the damaged wagon before the convoy loses its smelter slot.

checks.notes: Primary field repair check.
The repair is much harder without tools.
Keeps the fixer working under stray shots and debris.
Extra hands are genuinely helpful here.

success.summary: The convoy limps through but keeps the contract alive.

failure.summary: The ore misses the furnace window and the contract collapses into losses.

nodes.label: Deliver the manifest
nodes.summary: Turn over the ore tally and sign off the delivery with Ironwheel's clerk.

checks.notes: Good reporting softens minor losses.

success.summary: Ironwheel logs the run and pays the crew.

records.name: Catacomb Quietus
records.summary: The Highcrown Adventurers Guild needs a disciplined party to clear a sealed catacomb passage so scribes can recover burial records and relic inventories.

notes: Protective wards, blunt weapons, and shields are especially valuable against undead branch outcomes.
More people help hold the ossuary choke, but too many bodies complicate narrow-hall positioning.

classification.failureProfile: Undead escalation, injuries, and loss of relic access for the sponsoring scriptorium.

roleSlots.label: Ward Keeper
roleSlots.notes: Handles seals, light pressure, and aggro control.

roleSlots.label: Line Holder
roleSlots.notes: Pins the ossuary chokepoints and protects the ward keeper.

roleSlots.label: Restorer
roleSlots.notes: Cleanses rot, patch-heals, and stabilizes after a branch failure.

partySizeRules.effect: Understaffed parties face harsher attrition and weaker relic recovery.
Large parties raise torch smoke and formation friction in the narrow halls.

miscNotes: This quest has one of the sharper success-to-failure combat pivots in the current starter quest set.
A critical success prevents future random undead flare-ups in the same passage.

nodes.label: Seal the entry
nodes.summary: Reinforce the outer seal before the party breaks into the burial hall.

checks.notes: Primary warding and seal-stability check.
Needed to trace the seal correctly.
A defensive ward steadies the seal.

success.summary: The seal holds behind you and limits the undead surge.

failure.summary: The seal is sloppy and the dead stir more violently than expected.

nodes.label: Break the wight line
nodes.summary: Fight through the first rank of grave dead before they overwhelm the ward keeper.

checks.notes: Reliable blunt force and spacing control matter against skeletal defenders.
Interrupts the wight's lead howl.
Direct healing prevents attrition from tipping the branch.
A third body makes the chokepoint much safer.

criticalSuccess.summary: The party breaks the line fast enough to preserve the relic alcove.

success.summary: The dead are pushed back and the chamber opens.

failure.summary: You win the line slowly and the relic niche takes splash damage.

nodes.label: Secure the ledger niche
nodes.summary: Recover the burial ledgers and keep the last chamber from collapsing under corpse weight and panic.

checks.notes: Avoid damaging the records while the room shifts.
Helps anyone injured in the prior branch keep working.
Old stone can still slip.

success.summary: The ledgers come out intact and the seal can be restored.

failure.summary: Some ledgers are recovered, but part of the alcove is lost.

nodes.label: Return the relic logs
nodes.summary: Turn the recovered records over to the guild archivist and close the contract.

success.summary: The guild accepts the records and clears payment.

records.name: Counterfeit Ring Sting
records.summary: Aurelis civic watch and the merchant guild want a discreet crew to expose a counterfeit scrip ring before festival trade opens.

notes: Too many people are bad in the surveillance phase.
Paralyze, Sleep, Blink, and Fast Cast style casters create safer arrest branches.

classification.failureProfile: Spooked suspects disappear, counterfeit stock is moved, and the watch loses leverage.

roleSlots.label: Face
roleSlots.notes: Confirms the fake work and keeps the cover story together.

roleSlots.label: Soft Arrester
roleSlots.notes: Handles low-noise takedowns if the suspects bolt.

partySizeRules.effect: Extra people are actively bad during surveillance and increase the chance of burning the sting.

miscNotes: This is the cleanest example in the starter database of extra people being bad.
Goldsmithing does not replace social checks but confirms the evidence branch.

nodes.label: Watch the exchange
nodes.summary: Shadow the suspect runners without spooking them before the handoff.

checks.notes: Tracking routes and body language.
Too many bodies ruin the tail.
A steady ward helps a watcher keep cover when noticed.

success.summary: The suspects walk you straight to the dye cellar.

failure.summary: The tail turns hot and the crew must improvise before the evidence moves.

nodes.label: Test the coin and plates
nodes.summary: Confirm the counterfeit work before the arrest call is made.

checks.notes: Spotting soft strike marks and bad edge weight.
Maintaining the buyer cover story.

success.summary: The crew confirms the plates and catches the ring red-handed.

failure.summary: The fake is obvious, but the buyer mask starts to crack.

nodes.label: Rush the dye cellar
nodes.summary: Seize the plates and pin the ringleader before the cellar is torched or stripped.

checks.notes: Quietly drops a runner.
Control magic pins suspects long enough for shackles.
The ringleader may have a preplanned escape.

criticalSuccess.summary: The ring is taken cleanly with ledgers, plates, and witnesses intact.

success.summary: The plates are seized, though one runner slips the net.

failure.summary: The raid scatters the ring and forces a partial case filing.

nodes.label: Submit the plates
nodes.summary: Return the seized plates and witness notes to the civic watch.

success.summary: The watch closes the sting and pays out the warrant purse.

records.name: Smokehouse Extortion Turnover
records.summary: A dockside broker wants a compact crew to flip an extortion bookkeeper, seize the tally chest, and exit before the harbor bruisers regroup.

notes: This quest is explicitly structured like a small organized operation: planning slots, role discipline, materials, and failure branches compound fast.
Too few people weakens leverage in the extraction phase; too many people increase noise in the setup phase.

classification.failureProfile: Arrest, faction retaliation, or losing the tally chest to a harbor gang counterpush.

roleSlots.label: Inside Face
roleSlots.notes: Gets close to the bookkeeper and keeps the setup calm.

roleSlots.label: Lookout
roleSlots.notes: Tracks harbor patrols and warns the crew if the lane turns hot.

roleSlots.label: Muscle
roleSlots.notes: Turns intimidation into a clean extraction if things go loud.

partySizeRules.effect: Too few bodies make the extraction phase dangerous if the bookkeeper resists.
Every extra person increases noise, suspicion, and the chance of a patrol branch.

miscNotes: This is the most Torn-inspired starter quest in the repository so far.
Role discipline matters more than raw level if the crew wants the clean payout branch.

nodes.label: Brief the crew
nodes.summary: Assign the inside face, the lookout, and the fallback muscle before the tavern crowd thickens.

checks.notes: Three is ideal; four starts to get noisy.
The face needs a convincing pitch.
Bad timing can make the whole setup uglier.

success.summary: The crew gets its timing and roles straight before moving.

failure.summary: The crew goes in shaky, with a higher chance of a noisy extraction.

nodes.label: Stage the blackout
nodes.summary: Kill the right lamps, cut the alley sightline, and keep the smokehouse boys from seeing the crew form up.

checks.notes: A quiet control spell helps the face move once a watcher needs to be neutralized.
Can quietly drop the watchdog if needed.
More people are bad during setup.

criticalSuccess.summary: The crew owns the dark and gets the first move for free.

success.summary: The lane goes dim enough for the approach.

failure.summary: A lamp crashes and the block starts to wake up.

nodes.label: Turn the bookkeeper
nodes.summary: Convince, threaten, or disable the tally keeper before he burns the names or whistles for help.

checks.notes: Primary pressure check if the face is doing it clean.
A sharp threat display can break the bookkeeper without a full brawl.
Can quietly end the argument if things turn.
Here extra people are actually good.

success.summary: The bookkeeper folds and the tally chest changes hands.

failure.summary: The chest is seized, but the smokehouse calls bruisers to the lane.

criticalFailure.summary: The bookkeeper bolts and the harbor gang reaches the alley before the crew can reset.

nodes.label: Wash the tally chest
nodes.summary: Move the stolen tallies through a clean handoff before dawn and take the final purse.

checks.notes: A late patrol can still complicate the payout.

success.summary: The chest is washed, the broker pays, and the lane goes quiet again.

failure.summary: The payoff lands, but a patrol skim cuts into the final take.

records.name: Soundings of Ashen Reef
records.summary: After a major seasonal storm, Starfall Harbormaster's Office commissions fresh soundings of Ashen Reef's channels, breakers, draft-safe approaches, and ruin markers before fishing and commercial traffic intensify.

notes: The civic contract is ordinarily available without a level, class, skill, magic, item, or standing gate.
Navigation, seamanship, equipment, health, fatigue, and party support describe suitability rather than admission requirements.

classification.failureProfile: The field packet remains incomplete until all three survey sectors and the known ruin markers are verified.

miscNotes: This is a paid civic contract, but exact turn-in payment and all other consequences remain deliberately deferred.
Old charts, departure instructions, authorization, and arranged anchorage access are supplied on acceptance as narrative source facts, not inventory grants.
Stormglass Bloom is an incidental discovery during the final inspection, not an authored objective.

nodes.label: Inshore Approach
nodes.summary: Record the common approach from the Starfall side: soundings, breakers, shore bearings, and a usable draft-safe line.

success.summary: The inshore approach is recorded for the field packet.

nodes.label: Working Reef
nodes.summary: Survey the shallows most relevant to fishing and local craft: shelves, breakers, old markers, anchorable water, and dangerous crossings.

success.summary: The working reef soundings are recorded for the field packet.

nodes.label: Outer Passage
nodes.summary: Survey the exposed approach used by larger fishing craft, merchant tenders, patrols, and traffic forced wide by wind.

success.summary: The outer passage is recorded for the field packet.

nodes.label: Ruin Markers
nodes.summary: Verify the known visible and submerged ruins used as navigation bearings and hazards, leaving the completed field packet ready for later turn-in.

success.summary: All three survey sectors and the ruin markers are verified in the field packet.
